sessions.lever: STRUCTURAL: separate the loop sentinel from the red channel and write the loop as `while ((sent = tbl[0]) >= 0)`
sessions.note: THE WIN. Reading target around the inner_check label showed two things the m2c-shaped body got wrong: (a) target keeps the RED CHANNEL and the LOOP SENTINEL in DIFFERENT registers - the body's colour args come from $s7/$s6/$s3 while the sentinel lives in $v0; (b) at the label target reads tbl[0] TWICE, `lh $v0,0($s0)` for the test and `lhu $v1,0($s0)` for the next rect[0]. Our body conflated both into one `r`, which put the label in the wrong place - exactly what the two asmfix rules were compensating for. Giving the sentinel its own variable and writing `while ((sent = tbl[0]) >= 0)` puts the read at the label as target does, supplies the missing THIRD phantom slot, and holds the instruction count at 135: score 41 (HEAD) / 40 (previous candidate) -> 29, with frame 88 / vars 24 / regs 10 / args 24 and 135 insns all exactly target. This is also a SEMANTIC CORRECTION - the old body passed `r` to func_80048A7C, so from the second iteration onward it passed the previous tbl[0] instead of the red channel; target always passes $s7. EXPECTED SIDE EFFECT: the two asmfix rules for this function should become unnecessary; verify at the completion gate. Round 8 then tested the call-arg LUID lever (hoist-call-arg-local-flips-jal-delay) on the remaining scheduling cluster where target computes gpu_LoadImage's args early: naming both args first in the loop block, only the source address, or only the rect pointer are ALL INERT at 29; moving the rect stores after the arg locals regresses to 52 (loses the frame). Also measured: for(;;) forms with an explicit break give 131 insns / 69 - the while-with-assignment form is the one that matches; `sid` combined with the corrected loop overshoots to four slots (vars 32). src/text1a.c reverted; candidate.c updated.

sessions.lever: register-alloc-pure-c Step-0 (.greg dispositions + conflict lists) then Levers A-C, 10 forms
sessions.note: NO MOVEMENT; banked at 29. STEP-0 RESULT (the valuable part): the rotating values are pseudo 76 = r -> $s7 (matches target), 77 = g -> $s6 (matches), 78 = b -> $s2 (target wants $s3), 82 = yoff -> $s3 (wants $s4), 79 = outer -> $s4 (wants $s2). Pseudos 75-84 MUTUALLY CONFLICT - a single clique - so each takes the first free register in allocno-priority order. Ours allocates b, yoff, outer; target's order must be outer, b, yoff. The entire residual is therefore ONE PERMUTATION OF THREE ALLOCNO PRIORITIES, and any lever has to raise `outer` above `b` and push `yoff` last. LEVERS A-C, 10 forms, none flips it: colour birth order b,r,g (32) / g,b,r (39) / r,b,g (29); outer if/else arm swap (31); yoff assigned before xoff in both arms (31); `outer = outer + 1` long form (29 inert); an extra `outer` reference in each arm (29 inert, and contrived - not a form to keep); s16 outer (34, +4 insns); s16 yoff (29 inert). Frame and instruction count stay exact (vars 24 / 135 insns) throughout, so none of these regress the structure - they just do not move the priority order.
